analysis.title: FX Daily Snapshot: USD reverses US mid-term election losses as AI-equity sell-off intensifies
key_insights: AI-related equities sold off sharply. Nasdaq composite fell about 5.5% and Topix and Kospi each fell about 6% overnight. Nasdaq broke below its 200-day moving average (around 25,090) for the first time since March and April.
Nasdaq composite is just over 12% below last month's peak, versus a roughly 13.8% decline in the first three months of this year.
MUFG reads the sell-off as a delayed reaction to the US mid-term results. Strong Democratic performance raised concern that AI data centre build-out could be disrupted or face tighter AI regulation.
Nvidia fell over 9% and has reversed all of its year-to-date gains. Neocloud companies continue to underperform.

Microsoft is tightening oversight of some data centre projects and stepping away from ones it deems risky due to delays, regulatory snags and high costs. It is reportedly debating whether to sign new neocloud deals, and some leaders are reluctant to add third-party capacity.
FX spillover from the equity sell-off has been modest. AUD is down about 1.5% against USD since 4 November, also hit by the correction in energy prices including natural gas.
The best performing G10 currencies are the safe havens JPY, USD and CHF. The dollar index has reversed all of its initial losses since the mid-term results.

USD resilience is surprising given the unwinding of AI-investment confidence and the drop in energy prices on renewed optimism over a US-Iran deal. USD strength this year was supported by higher energy prices and record foreign demand for riskier US assets. If both reverse, USD weakening becomes more likely.

The equity sell-off is tightening US financial conditions, which Fed Chair Kevin Warsh acknowledged at the last FOMC meeting. Continued tightening could make a planned December Fed hike less likely, a downside risk for USD.

US rate markets price about 16bps of hikes by December, down from about 21bps on 4 November. A December hike is still judged more likely than not. MUFG says financial conditions may matter more for the December decision than today's NFP, which is expected to be stronger.
BoE delivered a hawkish hike. UK yields and GBP rose initially, then reversed as the US equity sell-off intensified. UK yields have held up better than in other major economies.

Governor Bailey said there is a strong case for another hike if the US-Iran conflict is not resolved. Mann, Pill, Greene and Lombardelli lean toward at least one more hike. Bailey rejected 'two-and-done' and said a series of hikes is 'not inevitable'.
MUFG forecasts another BoE hike in February next year but sees a higher risk of a back-to-back hike in December. UK markets price about 13bps of hikes by December.

The BoE's forecasts did not incorporate the recent sharp drop in oil. If oil stays low on progress toward a US-Iran deal, the BoE may hold off in December. A deeper AI sell-off and tighter global financial conditions could also dampen its willingness to tighten.

GBP is supported by stronger UK growth, higher UK yields and fiscal concerns being a bigger issue in the euro area. MUFG says the hawkish BoE should reinforce GBP bullish momentum into year-end. A deeper AI sell-off is the main downside risk since GBP behaves as a high-yielding G10 currency.

market_movers.rationale: Nvidia fell over 9% in the AI-related sell-off and has reversed all of its year-to-date gains. This is market color, not a rating call.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Expected to show stronger employment growth. MUFG says financial conditions may matter more than this print for the December Fed decision.
A December hike is still more likely than not, but the probability has dropped.
Market is attaching some chance of a back-to-back hike in December.

risk_factors: A deeper AI-related equity sell-off tightening financial conditions further, a downside risk for USD and GBP
Reversal of energy price strength and foreign demand for risky US assets, both of which supported USD this year
Disruption or tighter regulation of AI data centre build-out following the US mid-term results
Oil staying much lower, which could lead the BoE to hold off on another hike
Microsoft pulling back from risky data centre projects and neocloud deals
vol_and_positioning: Safe haven currencies (JPY, USD, CHF) are the best performing G10 currencies. AUD is the weakest, down about 1.5% against USD since 4 November.
Nasdaq composite is more than 12% below last month's peak after breaking its 200-day moving average.

tension_points.bull_case: USD is acting as a safe haven and has reversed all its post-election losses. The Fed still prices about 16bps of hikes, and NFP is expected to be stronger.
tension_points.bear_case: If energy prices and foreign demand for risky US assets both keep reversing, and tighter financial conditions make a December Fed hike less likely, USD could weaken.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued tightening of US financial conditions that makes a December Fed hike less likely, alongside further falls in energy prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Bailey said there is a strong case for another hike if the US-Iran conflict is unresolved. The majority of MPC leans toward at least one more hike, and MUFG sees a risk of a back-to-back hike in December.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil has dropped sharply and was not in the BoE's forecasts. A US-Iran deal and the AI-driven tightening of financial conditions could make the BoE hold off in December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil staying at much lower levels on progress toward a US-Iran deal.
